requirement_text: Have a 3.0 GPA in A-G courses taken in the 10th and 11th grade years. (3.4 GPA for non-residents)
limitations: The 3.0/3.4 split is by CA residency (resident vs. nonresident), not by domestic/international status -- an out-of-state US applicant is 'nonresident' (3.4 floor) but still domestic. Does not map cleanly onto applies_to=domestic/international, so recorded as 'both' with the residency distinction kept inside requirement_text.
researcher_notes: Corroborated identically on the UC systemwide page (admission.universityofcalifornia.edu/admission-requirements/freshman-requirements/: 'Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident)') -- a systemwide UC rule Berkeley restates, not a Berkeley-specific figure. Same Berkeley page states GPA is 'calculated using 10th and 11th grade UC-approved courses only' -- 12th-grade courses are reviewed for rigor/trend but excluded from the GPA calculation itself. No A-G course grade below C is allowed regardless of overall GPA (see UCB0002).

requirement_text: To meet minimum admission requirements, you must complete 15 yearlong high school courses with a letter grade of C or better, with at least 11 of the 15 completed by the end of 11th grade.
limitations: Merges two fetches: the exact '15 yearlong courses, C or better' sentence is verbatim from subject-requirement-a-g.html; the 'at least 11 by the end of 11th/junior year' detail was independently corroborated on admission.universityofcalifornia.edu/admission-requirements/freshman-requirements/ ('a minimum of 15 college-preparatory courses (A-G courses) with a letter grade of C or better,' 'with at least 11 completed by the end of junior year') -- combined here rather than kept as two rows since they describe one rule.
researcher_notes: See UCB0003-UCB0009 for the per-subject (A-G) breakdown. CHECKED FOR COLLEGE-SPECIFIC DIFFERENTIATION per this research pass's brief: no currently-published UC Berkeley admission requirement (as opposed to post-enrollment degree requirement or holistic-review emphasis) was found that differs by college (College of Engineering, College of Chemistry, Rausser College of Natural Resources, College of Environmental Design) from this systemwide A-G/GPA framework -- all Berkeley colleges/L&S divisions appear to share the same minimum eligibility floor, with selectivity differing by holistic review rather than by a distinct published requirement. A claim that Engineering/Chemistry freshman applicants need 'four years of mathematics, and chemistry and physics' as an admission requirement surfaced repeatedly in search results, traced consistently to nuc.berkeley.edu/Admissions/ (Nuclear Engineering department) -- EXCLUDED as a source: that page also references 'SAT I: Reasoning Test,' 'SAT II: Subject Test scores' (discontinued by the College Board in 2021) and 'Affirmative Action' as a factor in selection (barred in California public university admissions by Prop 209 since 1996), which are unambiguous staleness markers, so nothing from that page was used.

requirement_text: (A) History: Two years of history, including: one year of world history, cultures or historical geography, and one year of U.S. history or one-half year of U.S. history and one-half year of civics or American government.
limitations: Required years: 2. Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: (B) English: Four years of college-preparatory English that include frequent writing, from brainstorming to final paper, as well as reading of classic and modern literature.
limitations: Required years: 4. Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: (C) Mathematics: Three years of college-preparatory mathematics that include the topics covered in elementary and advanced algebra and two- and three-dimensional geometry; a fourth year of math is strongly recommended.
limitations: Required years: 3 (a 4th year is recommended, not required). Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: (D) Science: Two years of college-preparatory science, including or integrating topics that provide fundamental knowledge in two of these three subjects: biology, chemistry, or physics. A third year of science is recommended.
limitations: Required years: 2 (a 3th year is recommended, not required). Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: (E) Language Other than English: Two years, or equivalent to the 2nd level of high school instruction, of the same language other than English are required. A third year of course work is recommended.
limitations: Required years: 2 (a 3th year is recommended, not required). Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: (F) Visual and Performing Arts: One yearlong course of visual and performing arts chosen from the following disciplines: dance, music, theater, visual arts or interdisciplinary arts.
limitations: Required years: 1. Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: (G) College-Preparatory Elective: One year (two semesters), in addition to those required in 'a-f' above, chosen from the following areas: visual and performing arts (non-introductory level courses), history, social science, English, advanced mathematics, laboratory science and language other than English (a third year in the language used for the 'e' requirement or two years of another language).
limitations: Required years: 1. Part of the 15-course A-G minimum in UCB0002; each subject requires a C or better, same as the overall policy.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC subject requirement; UC Berkeley does not publish a Berkeley-specific override of the A-G subject pattern itself (unlike its TOEFL threshold, see UCB0013).

requirement_text: UC Berkeley is test-free, which means we will not use SAT/ACT test scores in any part of our application process. This includes not using scores as part of the campus's admissions selection process, nor as part of the scholarship process. Any scores submitted to UC Berkeley will be used for placement or subject credit purposes should the student be admitted.
limitations: Berkeley's own page uses 'test-free' rather than 'test-blind'; both terms describe the same practical rule here (SAT/ACT scores are not used anywhere in the admissions or scholarship decision, even if submitted) -- do not treat 'test-optional' language found on third-party sites as equivalent, since UC does not merely make scores optional, it ignores them entirely.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK (do not assume the private-university test-optional/test-required framing applies): confirmed this is UC-systemwide, not Berkeley-specific -- traces to the UC Board of Regents' May 2020 decision (universityofcalifornia.edu press release, archived text confirms a phased plan: test-optional 2021-22, test-blind for CA applicants 2023-24, and 'if by 2025 the new test is either unfeasible or not ready, consideration of the ACT/SAT for freshman admissions would still be eliminated' -- no replacement test was built, so full test-blind status took effect). STATUS AS OF RETRIEVAL IS ACTIVELY UNDER REVIEW BUT UNCHANGED FOR THE CURRENT CYCLE: UC's Academic Council directed BOARS (Board of Admissions and Relations with Schools) to conduct a faculty-led review after STEM faculty petitioned in 2026 to reinstate an SAT/ACT math requirement; official UC statement (universityofcalifornia.edu/press-room/statement-uc-academic-senate-chair-ahmet-palazoglu-boars-undergraduate-admissions-review, fetched this pass) explicitly says: 'Students applying by November 30, 2026, for fall 2027 admission will not be required to submit SAT or ACT scores, nor will any other applicant for admission for fall 2027' and 'There has been no change to UC's standardized testing policy at this time.' Review timeline per that same statement: BOARS report to Academic Council due February 12, 2027; Board of Regents recommendation no later than June 2027 -- i.e. any change would earliest affect the FOLLOWING cycle (fall 2028), not the one this record's cycle_year would represent. cycle_year left null because Berkeley's own test-free policy page carries no cycle label, but the fall-2027 currency is independently confirmed by the dated UC press statement above.

requirement_text: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) iBT or iBT Home Edition: Prior to January 2026 a minimum score of 80 or better.
limitations: Applies only to TOEFL iBT tests taken before 2026-01-21 (ETS's own scale-cutover date). This is the UC SYSTEMWIDE minimum; UC Berkeley itself sets a higher minimum on this same legacy scale (90, not 80) -- see UCB0013.
researcher_notes: SCALE TRAP CHECK per scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md: this is the pre-cutover 0-120 legacy scale, superseded going forward by UCB0012 (1-6 scale, effective 2026-01-21). Recorded as VERIFIED_HISTORICAL rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT because, as of this research pass's retrieval date (2026-08-21), all TOEFL sittings now fall on or after the 2026-01-21 cutover, making the 'prior to January 2026' threshold no longer reachable by any new test-taker -- kept for completeness and to prevent a later pass from re-surfacing it as current.

requirement_text: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) iBT or iBT Home Edition: Effective January 2026 a minimum score of 4.5 or better.
limitations: UC systemwide floor only; UC Berkeley's own page states a higher/differently-notated figure -- see UCB0013, which should take precedence for Berkeley-specific evaluation.
researcher_notes: Matches ETS's own announced rescale (new 1-6 scale, 0.5 increments, average not sum of the four section scores) documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md. No per-section/subtest minimum is published by UC systemwide for TOEFL -- this is an overall-score-only threshold, so it does not exhibit the Glasgow-style partial-unsatisfiability defect (no subtest minimum survives or fails to survive the rescale, because none is stated).

requirement_text: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) with a minimum score of 90/4.5 or better.
limitations: Unlike the UC systemwide page (UCB0011/UCB0012), this Berkeley-specific page does NOT date-anchor the two numbers to a before/after 2026-01-21 split -- it presents '90/4.5' jointly as if describing one current requirement. It is genuinely ambiguous whether '90' is (a) Berkeley's own higher-than-systemwide legacy-scale floor carried forward as a label even though no new test reports on that scale anymore, or (b) intended as the ETS 'comparable' 0-120 score that ETS supplies on score reports for two years after the cutover (through ~January 2028). Per scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md's recommended interim rule, an unqualified/undated TOEFL scale figure like this should evaluate to needs_manual_review rather than a confident met/not_met.
researcher_notes: This IS a genuine Berkeley-specific override of the systemwide floor (systemwide is 80 legacy / 4.5 new per UCB0011-12; Berkeley's own international-requirements page states 90/4.5), consistent with the systemwide page's own statement that 'A UC campus may require a score higher than the minimum for admission selection' (fetched this pass from the same systemwide English-proficiency page). Both numbers appearing jointly is treated here as Berkeley intending them as equivalent expressions of ONE current requirement (comparable-score reading), not as two temporally separate MIT-style thresholds -- but this reading is not fully certain, hence NEEDS_REVIEW rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT.

requirement_text: Score 6.5 or higher on the International English Language Testing System (IELTS). UC does not accept IELTS One Skill Retake to meet English proficiency requirements.
limitations: NAMED EXCLUSION per scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md trap #3: a numerically-qualifying 6.5 obtained via IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted -- a scalar comparison alone cannot detect this, since it depends on score PROVENANCE, not the number. No dedicated provenance field exists in this schema; flagged here in requirement_text and limitations per the doc's recommended interim treatment.
researcher_notes: IELTS 0-9 band scale is unaffected by the TOEFL rescale (confirmed unambiguous per the scale audit in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md). Berkeley's own international-requirements page (www.admissions.berkeley.edu/requirements-for-international-students/) restates the same 6.5 minimum with no Berkeley-specific override, unlike TOEFL (contrast with UCB0013).

requirement_text: Duolingo English Test (DET): Minimum score of 115.
researcher_notes: No Duolingo-specific value exists in this schema's test_scale enum (TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge/SAT only) -- left null rather than force-fit an inaccurate enum value, matching the MIT batch's treatment of PTE Academic for the same reason. Duolingo's native scale is 10-160; 115 is on that native scale. Berkeley's own international-requirements page restates the identical 115 figure -- no Berkeley-specific override found for this instrument (contrast with TOEFL, UCB0013).

requirement_text: You're not required to submit exam scores if you meet certain conditions. Demonstrate English proficiency by: scoring 3, 4 or 5 on the AP examination in English Language and Composition, or English Literature and Composition; or scoring 6 or 7 on the IB Standard Level examination in English (Language A only); or scoring 5, 6 or 7 on the IB Higher Level examination in English (Language A only); or ACT English Language Arts (ELA): score of 24 or higher; or SAT Writing and Language: score of 31 or higher; or earning a grade of C or better in a UC-transferable college course in English composition; or 3 or more years of Language of Instruction (LOI) in English.
limitations: Combines alternative pathways found across two fetches of overlapping UC systemwide and Berkeley-specific international-requirements pages (both listed the same alternatives); the '3+ years of Language of Instruction (LOI) in English' item was found on Berkeley's own www.admissions.berkeley.edu/requirements-for-international-students/ page specifically and not independently confirmed on the systemwide page fetched in this pass.
researcher_notes: Any ONE of these satisfies the requirement in place of a TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo score -- an 'OR' rule, not cumulative. Each sub-threshold (AP 3/4/5, IB SL 6/7, IB HL 5/6/7, ACT ELA 24+, SAT W&L 31+) is its own scale and is not decomposed into separate rows here to avoid fragmenting one coherent alternative-pathway rule into many near-duplicate records; a future ingestion pass may want to split these per-instrument if the evaluator needs to check them independently.

requirement_text: Applicants must finish secondary school and earn a certificate of completion which allows admission to a university in their home country or country of graduation. Students who have completed the IGCSE or O-level exams have not yet met the requirements for admission at UC Berkeley -- the university requires further study: either completion of the two-year A-level program with a minimum of three academic exams, the IB diploma program, or another similar academic curriculum.
limitations: Obtained via WebFetch summarization rather than raw page text; the IGCSE/O-level exclusion and the 'two-year A-level, minimum three academic exams' figure should be re-confirmed with a direct page read before treating the exact exam-count as authoritative, since this was not independently cross-corroborated on a second official page in this research pass.
researcher_notes: This is a genuine NAMED EXCLUSION in the scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md sense: a real, completed secondary credential (IGCSE/O-level) is explicitly stated as insufficient on its own, regardless of grades achieved -- a pure 'has the student finished secondary school' check would wrongly mark this met. Distinct from the A-G subject-matter requirements (UCB0002-0009), which describe subject/grade content; this describes credential-LEVEL sufficiency for applicants schooled outside the US A-G system.

requirement_text: All documents submitted (such as transcripts, bank statements, test scores, etc.) must be in English or officially translated into English or have an officially issued version in English. Students who have attended schools in other countries may require their transcripts to be authenticated by a credential evaluation agency to be told the equivalence in the United States.
limitations: Obtained via WebFetch summarization of a page found through search rather than a page independently corroborated twice in this pass; treat the credential-evaluation-agency clause as directionally correct but re-verify exact wording before quoting to a student as verbatim.
researcher_notes: Procedural/document-format requirement rather than an eligibility threshold -- included because it is a real gating condition on submitted evidence, consistent with this schema's 'international' category.

requirement_text: The Berkeley International Office requires documentation of sufficient funds for the first year of study, and submission of a Non-immigrant Information Form (NIF).
limitations: This reads as a visa/I-20 issuance requirement administered by the Berkeley International Office, which typically applies AFTER an admission offer (to issue immigration documents) rather than as a precondition for the admission decision itself -- recorded here because it appeared on an Admissions-office 'requirements for international students' page, but do not treat it as gating the admission decision the way GPA/A-G/testing do without further confirmation of exactly when in the process it is collected.
researcher_notes: No specific dollar figure for 'sufficient funds' was stated on the fetched page.

requirement_text: You must respond to only 4 of the 8 questions [Personal Insight Questions]. Each response is limited to a maximum of 350 words.
limitations: 350 words is a maximum, not a minimum -- no minimum length is stated.
researcher_notes: Systemwide UC requirement, applies identically at Berkeley (Berkeley's own PIQ page defers to this systemwide page rather than restating different rules). The 8 prompts, verbatim from the same page, for reference: 1. Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time. | 2. Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side. | 3. What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time? | 4. Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced. | 5. Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement? | 6. Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom. | 7. What have you done to make your school or your community a better place? | 8. Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?

requirement_text: Select applicants to UC Berkeley are invited to submit two letters of recommendation. Submission is voluntary and not required for full consideration of the application for admission. At least one letter should be written by a teacher or instructor in a core academic subject. Only students who have submitted a UC application will be considered for the letters of recommendation process.
limitations: Not all applicants are invited -- only a selected subset. A student cannot proactively opt in; unsolicited letters are explicitly not accepted ('we will not accept unsolicited letters or supplemental information'). Do not evaluate a missing recommendation as not_met for an applicant who was never invited.
researcher_notes: Deadline for invited applicants is January 10 (11:59 PM) -- see companion deadline record DL-2026-08-21-UCB0009. Invitations are sent 'October through early December' per the same page. Berkeley explicitly does not use the Naviance system for these letters.

requirement_text: UC Berkeley uses the UC Application (apply.universityofcalifornia.edu), not the Common Application. Apply to as many UC campuses as you like with one application. UC Berkeley does not offer early action or early decision options.
researcher_notes: TRAP CHECK per this research pass's brief (do not assume the private-university Common App / ED-EA pattern applies to UC campuses): CONFIRMED -- UC Berkeley (and all 9 undergraduate UC campuses) use the UC's own centralized application, entirely separate from the Common App, submitted once and routed to every UC campus the student selects. CONFIRMED there is no Early Decision / Early Action / Restrictive Early Action distinction at Berkeley or anywhere in the UC system -- a single filing period applies uniformly (see deadline record DL-2026-08-21-UCB0001). This was independently corroborated on both admission.universityofcalifornia.edu (systemwide) and admissions.berkeley.edu (Berkeley-specific) pages fetched in this pass, with no conflicting mention of an early round found anywhere.

requirement_text: The application fee is $80 per UC campus ($95 for international applicants), with fee waivers available for students meeting financial need criteria.
limitations: Fee is charged PER UC CAMPUS selected on the shared UC Application, not a Berkeley-specific fee -- a student applying to multiple UC campuses pays this amount once per campus. Exact fee-waiver eligibility criteria were not independently verified in this pass (not re-fetched from a dedicated fee-waiver page).

requirement_text: International students are ineligible for federal, state, and need-based university financial aid.
limitations: This is an ELIGIBILITY fact, not an admission-blocking requirement -- included because ORYN's brief for this pass explicitly asked for residency-based aid-eligibility distinctions to be recorded as their own requirement facts (public-university tuition/aid structures differ sharply by residency, unlike most private universities). International students should consult UC Berkeley's Financial Aid and Scholarships Office directly for external/departmental scholarship guidance, per the same source page.
researcher_notes: Contrast with UCB0025 (AB 540 / California Dream Act pathway), which covers a DIFFERENT population (certain non-FAFSA-eligible students who nonetheless meet California residency-track criteria) -- do not conflate 'international' with 'ineligible for FAFSA'; AB 540-eligible students are also ineligible for FAFSA but are NOT the population this record describes.

requirement_text: The California Dream Act extends financial aid eligibility to students who qualify for a nonresident tuition exemption under AB 540, including undocumented students. Eligible students may access state and UC financial aid, private scholarships, and DREAM Loan Program borrowing, but remain excluded from federal aid (federal loans, grants, and federal work-study). Students with DACA status should not fill out a FAFSA but should still fill out the Cal Dream Act application if anticipating AB 540 eligibility.
limitations: AB 540 eligibility itself (separate California law) generally requires attending a California high school for 3+ years and graduating from one (or equivalent), plus filing an affidavit with the campus -- the exact AB 540 criteria were found via a California Student Aid Commission-adjacent search summary, not independently re-verified on a UC-official page in this pass, so are not quoted verbatim here; only the Dream Act aid-access consequence (this record's requirement_text) was fetched from an official UC page directly. 'applies_to: domestic' reflects that AB 540 is a California-residency-track category distinct from international (F-1/J-1 visa) status, not a claim about citizenship -- the eligible population includes undocumented students, DACA recipients, T/U visa holders, and some citizens/lawfully-present residents who meet the 3-year California high school criterion.
researcher_notes: Genuinely distinct population and rule from both UCB0024 (international students, fully excluded from federal/state/institutional need-based aid) and ordinary FAFSA-eligible domestic students -- a three-way residency-based split, matching what this research pass's brief asked to check for. See deadline record DL-2026-08-21-UCB0003 for the Dream Act Application's own current-cycle deadline; note that THIS eligibility page's own stated filing-period dates were found stale at retrieval (still showing the closed Fall 2026 cycle) -- see DL-2026-08-21-UCB0005.
